claims.sourceText: Edgar Fouche's Military, and DOD contractors reference Documents, 15 pages read in full, https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The same collection carries an Air Training Command Associate in Applied Science degree in Avionics Systems Technology conferred July 1983 through the Community College of the Air Force, a 1970 Field Training Detachment certificate in Solid State Devices, and a February 1974 McDonnell Aircraft Corporation certificate for the F-15 Eagle Integrated Avionics Component Technicians Course. Every item in the collection is a decoration, a training certificate, a performance report, a degree, or one personnel assignment letter. There is no discharge certificate, no DD Form 214, no clearance record and no programme document.

claims.text: THE 'SAC/DARPA CLASSIFIED DOCUMENT' CARRIES NO CLASSIFICATION MARKING. The page 1 image, rendered at 190 dpi and read, reads: 'DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE / HEADQUARTERS STRATEGIC AIR COMMAND / OFFUTT AIR FORCE BASE, NEBRASKA 68113 / 10 JUL 1984 / REPLY TO ATTN OF: DARPA / SUBJECT: Request for Assignment [redacted] MSgt Edgar A. Fouche, FR[redacted] (Your Ltr, 21 Jun 84) / TO: LGMQ / HQ AFMPC has approved an AAR 51[redacted] on MSgt (32674) Fouche as requested. MSgt Fouche's date of availability is Aug 87. / DALE E. HAGERMAN, TSgt, USAF / NCOIC, Amn Acft Maint Asgns Sec / Dir of Asgns, DCS/Pers', with a handwritten marginal note reading '(Controlled) 51 still accessable until' and the Strategic Air Command motto at the foot. There is no banner marking, no portion marking, no control number and no copy-of count anywhere on the page. It is signed by a technical sergeant in an assignments section of a personnel directorate.

a.label: AF Form 77a, Letter of Evaluation, 24 August 1979

edges.label: Records temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3, the unit operating Groom Lake, 1 June to 14 August 1979
edges.note: TIER 2 IS THE CEILING AND HERE IS WHY. The form itself says 'AFFTC-DET 3, Nellis AF Range', which is Tier 1. The identification of DET 3 AFFTC with Groom Lake rests on Peter Merlin's own published site and not on any primary Air Force unit history, organisational chart or FOIA release opened by this research. The weaker link sets the tier.

edges.label: Claims assignment to 6515 TSS, AFFTC, Edwards AFB on the F-15 R&D and FOT&E programme
edges.note: His own statement in the caption layer: 'When I arrived at Edwards AFB - 6515 TSS - AFFTC, I was assigned to the F-15 R&D and FOT&E Program.' No form in the collection carries an Edwards assignment, and Andrew Johnson's account of the FOIA return does not list one. Tier 2 on his word.

edges.label: Documented ten weeks temporary duty in 1979, plus extensive first-person narration in the 1998 presentation
edges.note: The strongest documented connection between any TR-3B claimant and a real classified airfield, and it must be read with its own limit attached: the form does not say what he did there, referring that out to 'a separate report' that is not in the file, and everything else on the form describes F-15 avionics intermediate shop work. The extensive Groom Lake narration in the 1998 presentation, including helicopter flights and a mess hall conversation about an NSA system, is Tier 2 on his word alone.

edges.label: USAF master sergeant; twenty year avionics maintenance career, three Meritorious Service Medals
edges.note: Tier 1 and entirely ordinary. The citations describe F-15 and F-16 manual test stations, the TEWS-TITE electronic warfare bed-down, and a Strategic Air Command liaison post at Kelly AFB. The second Meritorious Service Medal citation closes 'culminate a distinguished career', which dates the end of active service to 1987.

a.label: Edgar Fouche's Military, and DOD contractors reference Documents

edges.label: Self-published compilation about and by its own subject
edges.note: INTENT: AUTHORSHIP AND SELF-PUBLICATION, mapped to research rather than custody so that the subject of a file is not given a x3.0 program edge to his own compilation. The compilation is about him, published by him, redacted by him on its own caption's admission, and one passage in it is signed 'My guess is he was a Staff Sergeant judging by his skills. - Ed Fouche'.

b.label: Edgar Fouche's Military, and DOD contractors reference Documents

edges.label: Reads the 'SAC/DARPA Classified Document' as an unclassified personnel letter from a personnel office
edges.note: Two parts of Merlin's reading were checked independently against the page image and hold: there is no classification marking of any kind on the letter, and the signature block does place the originating office inside the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel, which is what his five-letter-office-code reading of 'REPLY TO: DARPA' predicts. His gloss of AAR as After Action Review was not verified against any Air Force instruction.

edges.label: The Fouche file's DARPA invocation rests on a letter from a personnel office
edges.note: DARPA is the single most reused word in the Fouche corpus and the board's existing darpa node should carry this explicitly. The document that carries the invocation bears no classification marking, is signed by a technical sergeant in an assignments section of a personnel directorate, and is captioned by Fouche himself with the agency's name wrong, as 'Defense Advanced Research Agency'.
